축하합니다.forms: polite: 축하해요 · casual: 축하해 · humble: 축하드립니다
축하합니다.x: Happy birthday! This is a present for you.

쉰.forms: native · counting things, age · same before a counter (쉰 살, 쉰다섯 명)
쉰.x: My mother is fifty this year.
쉰.t: Native tens go on: 예순 60, 일흔 70, 여든 80, 아흔 90. For larger numbers Sino-Korean is far more common.

많다.x: There are really a lot of people in Myeongdong.
많다.e: 많이 = a lot; hosts say 많이 드세요 'eat a lot!'
많다.t: Pronounced [만타]; the ㅎ is silent before a vowel: 많아요 [마나요].

감기에 걸리다.forms: 감기에 걸렸어요 (I have a cold) · 감기에 걸리지 마세요 (Don't catch a cold)
감기에 걸리다.x: The weather suddenly got cold, and I caught a cold.
감기에 걸리다.e: 걸리다 means 'to be caught' or 'hooked': you get caught by a cold.
감기에 걸리다.t: Use the past tense for a cold you have now: 감기에 걸렸어요 = I have a cold.

성격.x: My younger sibling has a bright, easygoing personality.
성격.e: Literally 'nature's pattern' — the shape of who you are.
성격.t: 성격이 좋아요 means 'has a nice personality'; 성격이 급해요 means 'is impatient'.

남자 친구.ex: 제 남자 친구는 요리를 아주 잘해요.
남자 친구.x: My boyfriend is very good at cooking.
남자 친구.t: For a male friend who is not a boyfriend, Koreans say 남사친 or just 친구, since 남자 친구 implies romance.

아니면.forms: A 아니면 B = A or B; between two questions
아니면.x: Would you like coffee, or tea?
아니면.t: 아니면 is the everyday 'or' between questions; 또는 is more formal or written.

예술가.ex: 이 마을에는 젊은 예술가들이 많이 살고 있어요.
예술가.x: Many young artists live in this village.

유치원.ex: 제 동생은 집 근처 유치원에 다녀요.
유치원.x: My little brother goes to a kindergarten near our house.
유치원.e: Literally 'garden of little ones', a translation of German 'Kindergarten'.

창의력.e: Literally 'power to create ideas'. -력 = ability: 영향력, 능력.

조.ex: 그 회사는 작년에 매출이 1조 원을 넘었어요.
조.x: That company's sales passed one trillion won last year.
조.e: The next big unit after 억: 10,000억 = 1조.
조.t: Korean counts big numbers in groups of four zeros: 만 (10⁴), 억 (10⁸), 조 (10¹²). Don't confuse it with 조 (組) 'group, team', as in 조별 과제.

의료비.x: Having insurance lowers the burden of medical costs.

후보자.x: Last night the candidates appeared in a televised debate.
후보자.e: Literally 'person waiting to fill' a post; -자 = person.

분하다.m: resentful, bitter, mortified (at losing or being wronged)
분하다.x: We gave up a goal in the last minute, and it was so infuriating.

살며시.ex: 아기가 깰까 봐 문을 살며시 닫았어요.
살며시.x: I closed the door gently so the baby wouldn't wake up.

거들다.forms: 거들어요 · 거들었어요 · 거들 거예요 · 거드세요 (ㄹ drops)
거들다.m: to help out, to lend a hand; to chime in
거들다.ex: 저녁 준비하는 것 좀 거들어 줄래요?
거들다.x: Could you help out a bit with getting dinner ready?
거들다.t: Also means backing up someone's argument: 옆에서 말을 거들다.

가슴을 졸이다.forms: 가슴을 졸여요 · 가슴을 졸였어요 · 가슴을 졸일 거예요 · 가슴을 졸인 (+noun)
가슴을 졸이다.m: to be on edge, to be anxious, to hold your breath
가슴을 졸이다.x: I was on pins and needles waiting for my test results.
가슴을 졸이다.e: 졸이다 also means 'to boil down'—as if the heart is simmering with worry.
가슴을 졸이다.t: Same meaning as 마음을 졸이다; don't confuse 졸이다 with 줄이다 'to reduce'.

금메달.x: That athlete won a gold medal at the Olympics.

위자료.m: compensation for emotional distress; (divorce) settlement payment
위자료.ex: 법원은 남편에게 위자료 5천만 원을 지급하라고 판결했어요.
위자료.x: The court ordered the husband to pay 50 million won in compensation.
위자료.t: In divorce cases, 위자료 compensates for the breakup and is separate from 재산 분할 (property division).

우선시하다.x: My parents always put my health first.

궁핍하다.ex: 전쟁 후 많은 사람들이 궁핍하게 살았어요.
궁핍하다.x: After the war, many people lived in poverty.

별나다.ex: 세상에는 별난 취미를 가진 사람이 많아요.
별나다.x: There are many people in the world with odd hobbies.
별나다.t: Pronounced [별라다]; 별난 사람 is a common, slightly teasing way to say 'an odd one'.

가랑비에 옷 젖는 줄 모른다.forms: 가랑비에 옷 젖는 줄 모른다고 · 가랑비에 옷 젖는 줄 몰라요
가랑비에 옷 젖는 줄 모른다.m: small things add up before you notice; little losses pile up unnoticed
가랑비에 옷 젖는 줄 모른다.ex: 가랑비에 옷 젖는 줄 모른다고, 커피값이 한 달에 십만 원이 넘었어요.
가랑비에 옷 젖는 줄 모른다.x: Little things add up; my coffee spending went over 100,000 won a month.
가랑비에 옷 젖는 줄 모른다.e: Literally 'you don't notice your clothes getting wet in a drizzle.' 가랑비 = light drizzle.
nb: 개구리 올챙이 적 생각 못 한다

구심점.m: rallying point, center of unity, focal point
구심점.ex: 그 지도자는 국민 통합의 구심점 역할을 했습니다.
구심점.x: That leader served as the rallying point for national unity.
구심점.t: Pronounced [구심쩜]; 구심점이 되다 / 구심점 역할을 하다 are the usual patterns.

내림세.x: Gas prices started trending down this week.
내림세.t: 내림세로 돌아서다 (turn downward) is a common news phrase.

시가총액.x: The company's market cap topped 100 trillion won.
시가총액.t: Often shortened to 시총 in news and investor talk.

교착상태.ex: 남북 대화가 몇 년째 교착상태에 빠져 있습니다.
교착상태.x: Inter-Korean dialogue has been stuck in a deadlock for several years.

방백.ex: 배우가 방백으로 관객에게 자신의 속마음을 털어놓았어요.
방백.x: In an aside, the actor revealed his true feelings to the audience.
방백.e: Literally 'speaking to the side': other characters supposedly can't hear.

당쟁.ex: 조선 후기에는 당쟁이 심해서 정치가 혼란스러웠어요.
당쟁.x: In late Joseon, factional strife was so severe that politics was in chaos.

연거푸.forms: 연거푸 + verb: 연거푸 마시다, 연거푸 실패하다
연거푸.m: repeatedly, in a row, again and again
연거푸.ex: 그는 물을 연거푸 세 잔이나 마셨어요.
연거푸.x: He drank three glasses of water in a row.
연거푸.e: Built from 연 'in a row' + native 거푸 'again'; 거푸 alone means the same.

의제화.m: agenda-setting, putting an issue on the agenda
의제화.ex: 시민단체가 기후 문제를 의제화하는 데 성공했습니다.
의제화.x: Civic groups succeeded in putting climate issues on the agenda.
의제화.e: -화 = '-ization', a very productive suffix: 고령화, 세계화, 민주화.

어스름하다.ex: 날이 어스름해지자 거리에 불이 하나둘 켜졌어요.
어스름하다.x: As dusk fell, the lights came on one by one along the street.

불문율.ex: 우리 회사에서는 선배보다 먼저 퇴근하지 않는 것이 불문율이에요.
불문율.x: At our company, it's an unwritten rule not to leave before your seniors.

당동벌이.m: siding with your own faction and attacking others
당동벌이.ex: 정치권의 당동벌이 때문에 국민들이 실망하고 있습니다.
당동벌이.x: People are disappointed by politicians backing their own side and attacking the rest.
당동벌이.e: Literally 'band with the same, attack the different'.
당동벌이.t: Pronounced [당동버리] — the ㄹ carries over to the next syllable.
